faq.q: How is this different from a hyperscaler-run cost review?
faq.a: Hyperscalers optimise their own bill within their walls. We work multi-cloud, cover commitments across all three CSPs, and design the operating model — not just the savings list.

faq.q: Do you require a specific FinOps tool?
faq.a: No. We're consulting-led and tool-agnostic. Where the estate genuinely needs tooling beyond native, we'll recommend based on fit.

faq.q: Can you guarantee savings?
faq.a: We commit to a quantified, defensible opportunity ≥15% of in-scope run-rate by Week 5, with named owners. We do not operate a gain-share commercial model.

faq.q: Do you only work with multi-cloud clients?
faq.a: No. Single-cloud clients are often where we add the most value.

faq.q: We're mostly lift-and-shift — is this still for us?
faq.a: Yes. Lift-and-shift estates are where FinOps discipline pays back fastest.

faq.q: Why 6 weeks, not 3 months?
faq.a: Six weeks is the Jump Start cadence — enough for baseline + design + mobilisation. Elevation to Walk/Run is a follow-on engagement.

objectionHandling.objection: We already have a FinOps team.
objectionHandling.response: Great — we're not here to replace them. Most FinOps teams we meet are stuck in reporting mode because they lack the operating rhythm and executive air cover. We amplify them.

objectionHandling.objection: Our hyperscaler is doing this for free.
objectionHandling.response: Hyperscaler teams do great work within their walls. Ask them for a multi-cloud view or a recommendation to move workload off their platform — you'll see the limit.

objectionHandling.objection: We tried this two years ago and it didn't stick.
objectionHandling.response: That's the most common story we hear. The reason is almost always operating model, not analysis — no forum, no KPI, no engineering accountability.

objectionHandling.objection: Six weeks feels short for our estate.
objectionHandling.response: Six weeks is the assessment and mobilisation cadence. Realisation of the backlog is a separate 2–3 quarter engagement.

objectionHandling.objection: Can you do this for a fixed % of savings?
objectionHandling.response: No. Gain-share biases the analysis toward quick wins and away from durable discipline. We're fixed-fee; the value is in the operating model that keeps compounding.

faq.q: How is this different from FinOps?
faq.a: FinOps governs cloud infrastructure spend (compute, storage, network). TokenOps governs GenAI consumption (tokens, API calls, model inference). Different unit metrics, different optimisation levers, different stakeholders.

faq.q: We only use one AI provider.
faq.a: Even single-provider estates benefit from unit economics, consumption governance, and model selection optimisation. Most clients we see have more GenAI usage than they realise.

objectionHandling.objection: Our FinOps team can handle this.
objectionHandling.response: FinOps teams are excellent at cloud cost management. Token economics are fundamentally different — per-call pricing, model version dependencies, prompt length impact. We extend their capability, not replace it.

objectionHandling.objection: GenAI spend isn't material yet.
objectionHandling.response: That's the best time to set up governance — before it grows. Organisations that wait until GenAI is 10% of their cloud bill find governance 5x harder to retrofit.

objectionHandling.objection: Can't we just use the provider's cost dashboard?
objectionHandling.response: Provider dashboards show consumption. They don't show unit economics per use case, allocation to business functions, or the governance framework for who can spend what.

whyWeWin: First-mover advantage — TokenOps is a distinct offering, not a FinOps afterthought
Sibling to FinOps Excellence — same methodology, different unit metrics
Combines AI/ML understanding with cost governance discipline
Jump Start methodology — 6-week fixed scope, fixed price
